title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: What did *Endurance Environmental Solutions* change, and what were its facts? `[V]`
options: It held that installing monitoring technology is a permissive rather than mandatory subject of bargaining

It restored the clear-and-unmistakable-waiver standard, retroactively, in a case where a clause reserving the right to "implement changes in equipment" did not permit installing cameras in 400 trucks without bargaining
It required employers to give notice before deploying AI that affects bargaining-unit work
It held that a general management-rights clause is sufficient where the technology is not novel
questions.explanation: 373 NLRB No. 141, decided 10 December 2024, overruling *MV Transportation* (2019) and its contract-coverage test. The facts are the transferable part: your own clause almost certainly contains language of about that generality, and your technology is more capable than a dash camera.

questions.prompt: What did the rescission of GC 23-02 change? `[V]`
options: It removed the prosecutorial theory, not the statutory right — Section 7 did not move
It made intrusive electronic monitoring lawful
It reversed a Board decision on algorithmic management
Nothing, because General Counsel memoranda have no effect
questions.explanation: Both errors are available here and both are expensive. A practitioner who memorised the memo in 2024 is wrong today; one who concludes the exposure is gone is also wrong. A memorandum is a prosecutorial theory, and its withdrawal changes who brings a case, not whether conduct can interfere with protected activity.

questions.prompt: Why does the Board's three-vote convention matter to a planning assumption? `[V]`
options: Because a Board decision requires three votes to issue

Because the Board does not reverse precedent without three votes for doing so — so a two-member majority declined to overturn precedent in January 2026, and the confirmations of 7 August 2026 satisfied the condition
Because three votes are needed for a quorum, which the Board lacked for eleven months
Because the convention is written into the Act and cannot be departed from
questions.explanation: The convention is unwritten and it is real. Its effect for six months of 2026 was stability; its effect now is that the standards restored by the previous majority are genuinely in play. Note that quorum — three sitting members — is a different requirement, which is answer C's trap.

questions.prompt: Your organisation expects the waiver standard to loosen. What follows for a change you implement now? `[V]`
options: You may implement now and rely on the expected standard, since the change post-dates the shift in composition
Nothing follows — the standard applies only prospectively either way
The change is judged under whatever standard exists when the case is decided, and doctrine in this line has been applied retroactively — so betting on a reversal is not a legal position
You should implement now, because conduct during a period of doctrinal uncertainty is not actionable
questions.explanation: *Endurance* itself applied retroactively. The asymmetry is worth internalising: a reversal helps you prospectively and tells you nothing about what you did while waiting for it.

questions.prompt: What is settled, and what is not, about the duty to bargain over AI? `[V]`
options: Both are settled — AI touching terms and conditions is a mandatory subject and the Board has so held
Neither is settled, since AI is not addressed anywhere in the Act
Settled that a change to terms and conditions is a mandatory subject that cannot be changed unilaterally; not settled because no Board decision applies it to an AI deployment
Settled by the SAG-AFTRA charge against Llama Productions
questions.explanation: A strong inference from settled doctrine, with a pending charge and no holding. Secondary sources routinely state the conclusion as law. The practical answer does not depend on resolving it: bargain it, or negotiate explicit language.

questions.prompt: Which provision has a union already negotiated that restates this curriculum's assist-versus-decide line? `[V]`
options: CWA's notice requirement at ZeniMax when AI implementation affects bargaining-unit work
The UPS–Teamsters prohibition on using sensor data as the sole basis for discipline, with required human review of context
NewsGuild-CWA's AI language across roughly 85–90 agreements
A requirement that employers disclose the training data of any performance-scoring model
questions.explanation: The distinction you have been learning as professional craft is, in some workplaces, a contractual obligation enforceable through grievance and arbitration. A is real and is the most common kind of provision; it is a notice term, not an assist/decide term.

questions.prompt: What is the convergence the module identifies, and why is it useful? `[V]`
options: Board doctrine and General Counsel priorities converge under a single administration

Notice, human review and records are both what the AI employment statutes keep landing on and what unions are winning at the table — so building all three satisfies several sources of obligation at once
US and EU law are converging on a single standard for algorithmic management
Contract and statute converge because collective agreements incorporate statutory minimums
questions.explanation: And in a represented workplace you may owe them years before a regulator asks, enforceable by grievance rather than investigation. Which makes your collective bargaining agreement an AI compliance document that somebody should read on purpose.

questions.prompt: Why is this module not conditional on having a represented population?
options: Because non-union employers are covered by the same Board rulemaking
Because protected concerted activity under Section 7 does not require a union, and the rescission of GC 23-02 removed the theory rather than the section
Because non-union workplaces are subject to the duty to bargain once a majority signs cards
Because *Weingarten* applies to unrepresented employees
questions.explanation: Concluding a non-union workplace is outside all of this is the layer error in its most expensive form. And D is the trap: *Epilepsy Foundation* (2000) extended *Weingarten* to unrepresented employees and *IBM Corp.* (2004) withdrew it, which is where the doctrine sits — a good illustration of how the doctrine layer behaves over twenty years.
